content:
From today, WhatsApp Web users can view, review and annotate PDF files without leaving the conversation. Here are the details.

Adobe Acrobat officially arrives on WhatsApp Web

Previously, when users received PDF files on WhatsApp, they had to download the file before opening it, and there were no built-in tools for reviewing or annotating documents.

Adobe announced today (yesterday) that its Acrobat PDF tools have been directly integrated into WhatsApp Web and the Windows version of the WhatsApp application, allowing users to open, review, and annotate documents without downloading files or leaving the conversation.

The company stated that in addition to regular PDF files, this integration also supports password-protected documents, and files shared in conversations continue to be protected by WhatsApp's end-to-end encryption. Adobe noted that "this means only conversation members can read their contents."

Adobe pointed out that this integration reflects the growing number of users using WhatsApp on larger screens to handle tasks such as reviewing contracts, invoices, forms, and homework, while also reflecting its broader strategy of bringing Acrobat's PDF tools to platforms where users work daily, such as Chrome, Microsoft 365 and Copilot, ChatGPT, Workday, and more.
